transcript.text: My indesit washing machine fills with water and drains but the drum just doesn't go round at all. Its an IWC something. Had it about 9 years. Is it worth fixing?

At nine years old, an Indesit washing machine often still has value if the fault is mechanical rather than electronic. The most common reason for filling and draining but not spinning (or agitating) on these models is a broken drive belt or worn motor brushes. If it's just the belt, it is usually worth fixing as it is cheap and straightforward; if it is the motor brushes, that is also a relatively low-cost repair. However, if the drum bearings have failed (usually indicated by a loud grinding noise), it is generally not worth repairing. To help us decide, please check if there is a belt visible at the back of the machine and let me know if you hear any buzzing sounds when it tries to start.

I took the back panel off and the belt is on both pulleys and feels tight, so it doesn't look broken. When it should be turning I can hear relays clicking but no buzzing or any other motor noise. I did notice a faint hot electrical smell a few weeks ago, but not since.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. To help them prepare, could you please read the model number from the sticker inside the door rim or on the back of the door?
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
I've looked at the label inside the door and it reads IWC 71252. That's as much as I can make out. Is the smell really a reason to scrap it, though? It was only faint and I haven't noticed it since.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A faint hot electrical smell is not something to ignore, even if it hasn't happened since. It usually means components like the motor's carbon brushes are wearing down and sparking internally, generating heat. Because there is an active safety hazard involving potential overheating or electrical arcing, it is not safe to use the machine again until a qualified engineer has inspected and repaired it internally.

candidates: Drive belt broken or slipped off (high)
Motor brushes worn out (common in 9-year-old Indesits) (medium)
